To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the flow of fluid generated by the rotation of cilia is sensed by the primary cilia of the left lateral plate mesoderm and that the calcium signal generated in the cilia is propagated to the left lateral plate cells by the release of extracellular calcium.
the flow of liquid is sensed by the node, that the flow is sensed by the calcium concentration gradient, and that the calcium concentration gradient is sensed by the cilia.
the flow is not required for left right asymmetry but is required for the normal development of the heart, and that the flow is required for the correct positioning of the heart.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of calcium in the development of left right asymmetries.

the mechanisms by which the leftward flow of extracellular fluid generated by clockwise rotating cilia in the node of the early mouse embryo, is converted into a molecular signal that specifies left right asymmetries of the embryo.
the mechanisms by which the leftward flow of extracellular liquid is translated into left-right asymmetric gene expression in the mouse embryo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ciliary rotation generates a leftward fluid flow, that the flow is interpreted by the heart as an asymmetric calcium gradient, which in turn is interpreted as a leftward flow and the flow is interpreted as left right asymmetry by the lateral plate mesoderm.

cilia drive the leftward flow of fluid, that the leftward flow is sensed by the node, that the left side of the node is then signaled to the lateral mesoderm and that the lateral mesodermal cells then interpret the signal and respond by initiating the expression of the left sided genes that will ultimately specify left right asymmetry in the developing body.
the leftward flow of fluid generated by the clockwise rotation of the cilia is interpreted as a signal that the left side of the body is different from the right.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cilia and calcium signalling are the key players in the process.
calcium is the key.
the cilia beat in a leftward direction, and the leftward flow of fluid drives a leftward calcium wave.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the flow of calcium ions through calcium channels in the cilia of the node may play a role in the interpretation of the flow of liquid.
calcium signalling is an essential part of the mechanism.
the calcium signal that initiates left right asymmetry is a transient signal, not a steady state, and that the calcium signal is not the sole determinant of asymmetry.
